lessons.claim: ★★ The governing (longest) relaxation time of a many-body system is not γ/κ built from a representative stiffness but **the lowest eigenvalue of the stiffness matrix**, γ/λ_min. chain-bend used τ_chain = γ/κ_center as the governing scale while τ_max = γ/λ_min is 9.18x longer (λ_min=526.4 vs κ_center=4830.7 kT/d²). Two things went wrong at once -- (a) De was underestimated 9.18x, so the 'De 0.1~10 sweep' was actually 0.99~91.8 and **never entered the quasi-static plateau at all** (it was a sweep that could not produce the saturating curve the sketch asked for) (b) the equilibration of 20 τ_chain = 2.2 τ_max was insufficient, leaving 11% residual transient and putting K* up to 21% out. Confirmed by measurement: raising the equilibration to 10 τ_max cut the block scatter **1000-fold** (σ 5785→0.7) and moved K′ by 21%. Setting dt from λ_max while not looking at λ_min is the trap -- it comes free from the same eigendecomposition.
